abstract: We introduce a simple diagrammatic approach for estimating how a randomly walking quantum particle searches on a graph in continuous-time, which involves sketching small weighted graphs with self-loops and considering degenerate perturbation theory’s effects on them. Using this method, we give the first example of degenerate perturbation theory solving search on a graph whose evolution occurs in a subspace whose dimension grows with $N$.

specification.problem: Spatial search by continuous-time quantum walk on a graph of N vertices: a particle evolving under a walk Hamiltonian plus a marked-vertex oracle term should concentrate amplitude on the marked vertex w, and the paper proposes a diagrammatic degenerate-perturbation-theory method to estimate the critical jumping rate, eigenvalue gap and runtime, including a graph whose invariant evolution subspace grows with N.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Scoped to the standard continuous-time quantum-walk search Hamiltonian and the generic degenerate-perturbation-theory estimate of the critical jumping rate and runtime, instantiated on the smallest nontrivial explicit case: the complete graph K_4 (N=4, one marked vertex, 2-qubit vertex register). The paper's specific contributions - the diagrammatic sketching of small weighted graphs with self-loops, and the particular graph whose evolution subspace dimension grows with N - are NOT reconstructed because the abstract gives no definitions for them.

equations.label: Continuous-time quantum walk search Hamiltonian
equations.description: Standard search Hamiltonian: a walk term proportional to the adjacency matrix plus a rank-one oracle marking vertex w. The paper may instead use the Laplacian L = D - A; for regular graphs the two choices differ only by a constant shift.
equations.justification: The abstract refers to a randomly walking quantum particle searching a graph in continuous time, which is the Childs-Goldstone spatial-search framework; the explicit form is recalled from background, not stated in the abstract.
assumptions: Adjacency-matrix form of the walk (Laplacian form not excluded by the abstract)

equations.label: Initial equal superposition
equations.description: The walker starts in the uniform superposition over vertices, the standard initial state for spatial search.
equations.justification: Standard initial state for continuous-time quantum-walk search; not stated in the abstract.

equations.label: Perturbative split for degenerate perturbation theory
equations.latex: H = H^{(0)} + V,\quad H^{(0)} = -\gamma A,\quad V = -|w\rangle\langle w|
equations.description: The oracle is treated as a perturbation of the walk Hamiltonian. At a critical \gamma, two (or more) eigenstates of H^{(0)} become degenerate; degenerate perturbation theory then diagonalizes V in that degenerate subspace.
equations.abstract_quote: considering degenerate perturbation theory’s effects on them
equations.justification: The abstract says degenerate perturbation theory is applied to the search problem; the natural (and standard) split is walk term as unperturbed Hamiltonian and oracle as perturbation. The specific unperturbed eigenstates and the diagrammatic weighted-graph picture are not given.
assumptions: Oracle term is the perturbation; walk term is unperturbed

equations.label: Leading-order degenerate perturbation theory and runtime
equations.latex: H_{ab} = \langle \psi_a | H | \psi_b \rangle,\ a,b \in \{1,\dots,d\};\quad \Delta E = E_{+} - E_{-};\quad t_* \approx \frac{\pi}{\Delta E}
equations.description: Within the d-dimensional degenerate eigenspace of H^{(0)} at the critical \gamma, the perturbed eigenstates are obtained by diagonalizing the d x d matrix H_{ab}. If |s\rangle and |w\rangle are each approximately a superposition of the two resulting lowest eigenstates with energies E_\pm, the evolution rotates |s\rangle to |w\rangle in time approximately \pi/\Delta E (approximation, not exact equality).
equations.justification: Generic degenerate-perturbation-theory estimate of the gap and runtime used in quantum-walk search analyses; recalled from background.
assumptions: Initial and marked states lie predominantly in the span of the two relevant eigenstates

equations.label: Tiny explicit instance: complete graph K_N with N=4
equations.latex: A = J - I,\quad \gamma_c = \frac{1}{N},\quad \Delta E \approx \frac{2}{\sqrt{N}},\quad t_* \approx \frac{\pi\sqrt{N}}{2},\quad p(t_*) \approx 1;\quad N=4:\ \gamma_c = \tfrac{1}{4},\ t_* \approx \pi
equations.description: Proposed smallest instance: complete graph on 4 vertices (J is the all-ones matrix). Known background results for complete-graph search: critical jumping rate 1/N, gap 2/\sqrt{N}, runtime \pi\sqrt{N}/2 with success probability approaching 1 asymptotically. This instance has a 2-dimensional invariant subspace span{|w\rangle,|s\rangle}, so it does NOT exhibit the paper's growing-dimension feature.
equations.justification: No scope was supplied, so a minimal explicit instance is chosen; complete-graph values are standard results, and the N=4 numbers follow from them (asymptotic approximations, so finite-N values are approximate).
assumptions: Instance choice K_4 is the reconstructor's, not the paper's
Asymptotic formulas applied at small N are approximate

equations.label: Success probability
equations.description: Probability of measuring the marked vertex after evolving for time t; the algorithm measures at t = t_*.
equations.justification: Standard definition of success probability for continuous-time search.

registers.name: vertex
registers.role: Encodes the vertex index v in binary (big-endian, |v\rangle = |v_1 v_0\rangle with v = 2 v_1 + v_0); the walker's position.

steps.description: Prepare the uniform superposition over vertices (for N=4: Hadamards on both qubits).
Fix the jumping rate at the critical value predicted by degenerate perturbation theory (for K_4: \gamma_c = 1/4) and form the search Hamiltonian.

Evolve under e^{-iHt} for time t_* \approx \pi/\Delta E (for K_4: t_* \approx \pi); the exponential may be realized by exact diagonalization in simulation or by Trotterization of the walk and oracle terms (assumption).
Measure the vertex register in the computational basis.

specification.measurement: Computational-basis measurement of the vertex register at time t_*; the outcome is a vertex label v, success if v = w.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Repeat the experiment to estimate p(t_*) as the fraction of runs returning w; compare with the perturbation-theory prediction (approximately 1 for the complete graph).
assumptions: No experiment_scope was supplied; the smallest useful construction (complete graph K_4, one marked vertex, 2 qubits) was chosen by the reconstructor
Adjacency-matrix form of the walk Hamiltonian is assumed; the paper may use the Laplacian
Leading-order degenerate perturbation theory suffices to predict the gap and runtime
Hamiltonian simulation method (exact exponentiation vs Trotterization) is left to the circuit stage
